extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (design patent practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining design patent applications under 35 U.S.C. 101/102/103/171/115/172 and related rules, including form paragraphs, prior art/date rules, and the proper factual/legal inquiries for novelty and nonobviousness of designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates which can be used for 35 U.S.C. 102(d) purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Date(s) Which Can Also Be Used for 35 U.S.C. 102(d) Purposes (INID Code (24)) vary by country/organization (e.g., protection starts on date of publication of design in official gazette; date of registration or grant which is the filing date; date of prior disclosure declared on deposit; date of design creation for design right jurisdictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the country-specific date specified (publication, registration/grant, filing date, deposit declaration, creation date, etc.) when asserting 35 U.S.C. 102(d) bars. Minimum requirements or special comments (e.g., deposit fees, proof of creation) noted for certain jurisdictions should be observed when relying on those dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) (foreign filing more than 6 months before U.S. filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as modified by 35 U.S.C. 172 should only be made when the examiner knows that the application for foreign registration/patent actually issued before the U.S. filing date based on an application filed more than six (6) months prior to filing in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grant of foreign registration/patent is not evident from the U.S. record or charts, include the prescribed form paragraph (¶ 15.03.01.fti) in the first action on the merits. In form paragraphs insert appropriate country names in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application examined under AIA first inventor to file provisions (¶ 15.10.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph to indicate the present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in any application subject to AIA first inventor to file provisions. Precede certain other form paragraphs with this one when required by filing/priority dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application examined under pre‑AIA first to invent provisions (¶ 15.10.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph to indicate the present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the pre‑AIA first to invent provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in any application filed on or after March 16, 2013 that is subject to the pre‑AIA prior art provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice re prior art available under both pre‑AIA and AIA (¶ 15.10.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the determination of whether an application is subject to AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 is incorrect, correction of statutory basis will not be a new ground of rejection if prior art and rationale would be the same under either status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be used in all Office Actions when a prior art rejection is made in an application with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claims priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013. Use only once in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) Rejection (AIA) - Anticipation (¶ 15.11.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated because the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the reference applied in the bracket. For applications with priority/benefit to before‑March‑16‑2013 filings, precede this paragraph with 15.10.aia and 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) Rejection - Anticipation (¶ 15.11.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) as being anticipated because the invention was known or used by others in this country, or patented or described in a printed publication in this or a foreign country before the invention thereof by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the applied reference in the bracket. For applications with effective filing date on/after March 16, 2013 but claiming priority to earlier filings, precede with 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) Rejection - >1 year statutory bar (¶ 15.12.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being anticipated because the invention was patented or described in a printed publication, or in public use or on sale in this country more than one (1) year prior to the application for patent in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the reference applied. For applications with priority claims to pre‑March‑16‑2013 filings, precede with 15.10.15 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) Rejection - Abandonment (¶ 15.13.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the appropriate reference/basis in the bracket when invoking abandonment as the statutory basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)/35 U.S.C. 172 Rejection - Applicant/patent in foreign country (>6 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d), as modified by 35 U.S.C. 172, as being anticipated because the invention was first patented or caused to be patented, or was the subject of an inventor’s certificate by the applicant (or assigns) in a foreign country prior to the U.S. application date on an application filed more than six (6) months before the U.S. filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the reference applied. This rejection only applies when foreign application was filed >6 months before U.S. filing and foreign protection matured before the U.S. filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) Rejection (AIA) - Anticipation by another's patent/application (¶ 15.15.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by a patent or an application published or deemed published under section 122(b) that names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the reference in the bracket. For claims with priority to earlier filings, precede with 15.10.aia and 15.10.15. This rejection may be overcome by specific showings (e.g., derivation, priority/benefit claims, prior public disclosure, common ownership statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) Rejection - Anticipation by earlier US application/patent (¶ 15.15.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated because the invention was described in a patented or published application for patent by another filed in the United States before the invention thereof by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the applied reference. For applications with later filing dates but priority to earlier filings, precede with 15.10.15 where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) Rejection - Not invented by applicant (¶ 15.16.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 because applicant did not himself invent the subject matter sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the basis supporting conclusion that applicant is not the inventor in the bracketed explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) Rejection - Prior invention by another (¶ 15.17.aia / ¶ 15.17.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 (g) because, before the applicant’s invention thereof, the invention was made in this country by another who had not abandoned, suppressed or concealed it. (AIA form notes similar contexts where pre‑AIA claims are present.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application claims or previously contained claims with effective filing dates before March 16, 2013, precede with appropriate form paragraphs (15.10.aia or 15.10.fti and 15.10.15). Explain supporting evidence in bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper inventorship — 35 U.S.C. 171 and 35 U.S.C. 115 (¶ 15.09.02.aia / ¶ 15.09.03.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that does not set forth the correct inventorship is subject to rejection under 35 U.S.C. 171 and 35 U.S.C. 115; 35 U.S.C. 115(a) requires the application to include the name of the inventor for any invention claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the basis for concluding inventorship is incorrect in the bracket. Use form paragraph 15.07.01 for rejections based on improper inventorship and precede these paragraphs as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical claim: common assignee — priority/identical-invention issue (¶ 15.24.05.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is directed to the same invention as that of the claim of a commonly assigned copending application, the issue of priority under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f)/(g) must be resolved, and the assignee is required to state which entity is the prior inventor of the conflicting subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer has no effect on this priority‑of‑invention refusal. Failure to state the prior inventor will result in holding the application abandoned. Include this paragraph after the form paragraph setting forth the 35 U.S.C. 102 rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of rejection — substantial similarity of appearance (¶ 15.15.01.aia / ¶ 15.15.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an explanation that the appearance of the cited reference is substantially the same as that of the claimed design (e.g., citation to International Seaway Trading Corp. v. Walgreens Corp.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explanatory paragraph should be included after the relevant 35 U.S.C. 102 rejection paragraph to explain the basis of the rejection and identify the applied reference in the bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection over copending application with common inventor/assignee (¶ 15.15.02.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) when a copending application (with a common inventor or assignee) discloses the design and would constitute prior art if published or patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection may be overcome by: (1) a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the disclosure was derived from the inventor (not prior art); (2) perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119; (3) perfecting benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 via ADS/1.78 reference; (4) a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of prior public disclosure; or (5) a statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) of common ownership/assignment/joint research agreement. This rejection may not be overcome by a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection — design disclosed but not claimed in copending application (¶ 15.15.02.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisionally reject under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) when a copending application (with common inventor/assignee) discloses the claimed design but does not claim it, based on a presumption of future publication or patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest possible ways to overcome: (A) show under 37 CFR 1.132 that the design was derived from the designer of this application; (B) show a date of invention prior to the reference under 37 CFR 1.131(a); (C) perfect priority under 35 U.S.C. 119; or (D) perfect benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 with specific reference filings complying with 37 CFR 1.78 and enablement/description requirements. Terminal disclaimer cannot overcome (In re Bartfeld). Also follow guidance for determining the proper 102(e) date (AIPA/pre‑AIPA nuances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) provisional rejection — design claimed in earlier‑filed design patent application with common inventor/assignee (¶ 15.15.03.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by a claim in a copending design patent application that has a common inventor or assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the different inventive entity and pre‑AIA date, it would constitute prior art if patented. The rejection may be overcome by abandoning the earlier‑filed copending application. Precede with 15.24.05.fti as appropriate and advise when 15.10.15 is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) rejection — design disclosed in a patent (¶ 15.15.04.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by a patent that names another inventor and has an earlier effectively filed date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by the same five showings listed for other 102(a)(2) provisional rejections (derivation, priority under 119, benefit under 120, 1.130(b) disclosure, or common ownership statement). Identify patent number in bracket. For design disclosed in earlier‑filed patents, consider subcombination/unclaimed matter issues and whether the earlier patent discloses the claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection — design disclosed but not claimed in a patent (¶ 15.15.04.fti and discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the claimed design is disclosed in the drawings of an earlier‑filed patent but not claimed therein; the earlier patent may render the design anticipated under pre‑AIA 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claimed design is disclosed in earlier patent drawings (possibly as subcombination or broken‑line matter), explain basis of rejection in brackets and follow instructions regarding priority/benefit paragraphs as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection maintained — subsequent action (¶ 15.38)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a second or subsequent action, if applicant's arguments have been considered and are not persuasive, include the 'Rejection Maintained' paragraph indicating the rejection under the cited statutory basis remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using, identify the reference(s) (in brackets). Suggest ways to overcome the rejection (e.g., show derivation, establish earlier date of invention, perfect priority/benefit) as appropriate in the examiner's explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection under other statutory provisions (¶ 15.40.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph for final rejection under statutory bases other than the 102/103 paragraphs, indicating the claim is finally rejected under [statute] for the stated reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert statutory basis and reasons in brackets. See MPEP Chapter 700 for procedures concerning 'Action is Final' and 'Advisory after Final' paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonobviousness evaluation — Graham factual inquiries applied to design patents (§ 1504.03 introductory)
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic factual inquiries from Graham v. John Deere (1966) apply to design patent nonobviousness: (A) determine scope and content of the prior art; (B) ascertain differences between the claimed invention and the prior art; (C) resolve the level of ordinary skill in the art; and (D) evaluate any objective evidence of nonobviousness (secondary considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four inquiries to gather facts. After fact‑finding, determine whether a prima facie case of obviousness exists by checking whether all claim limitations are taught or suggested by the prior art and whether the overall appearance would have been obvious to a designer of ordinary skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the prior art in design cases — analogous arts and ornamentation (§ 1504.03 A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of relevant prior art for design obviousness extends to all 'analogous arts.' In design cases, analogous arts analysis focuses on whether ornamental features in one article would suggest application to another (In re Glavas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the problem is providing attractive appearance to a surface, the nature of the underlying article may be immaterial (e.g., wallpaper vs oven door vs crockery). If differences involve shape/form (material modifications), the nature of the articles must be considered. Where differences are limited to surface ornamentation, prior art with substantially the same ornamentation is analogous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences between prior art and claimed design — identify all differences and address de minimis distinctions (§ 1504.03 B)
rubrics_metrics.description: All differences between the claimed design and the closest prior art reference should be identified in any rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103. Mere existence of differences is not alone sufficient for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any differences are considered de minimis or inconsequential from a design viewpoint, the rejection should state that. Cite relevant case law (e.g., In re Lamb) when explaining why differences do or do not support patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of ordinary skill in the art for design patents (§ 1504.03 C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The level of ordinary skill for evaluating design obviousness is from the perspective of the 'designer of ... articles of the types presented' (cases such as In re Nalbandian and In re Carter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame obviousness inquiry in terms of what a designer of ordinary skill in the relevant article type would find obvious given the prior art and the overall appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evidence of nonobviousness (secondary considerations) (§ 1504.03 D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary considerations such as commercial success and copying of the design by others are relevant evidence in the nonobviousness inquiry and may be presented at prima facie evaluation or in rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider and, where present, evaluate evidence like commercial success, copying, long-felt need, failure of others, licensing, and recognition. See MPEP § 716 et seq. and relevant case law (e.g., MRC Innovations v. Hunter Mfg.; Crocs Inc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie obviousness for design claims — overall appearance and claim limitation teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a prima facie case of obviousness for a design claim, the overall appearance of the design must be considered and all claim limitations must be taught or suggested by the prior art. The proper standard is whether the design would have been obvious to a designer of ordinary skill with the claimed type of article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After applying the Graham inquiries and considering analogous arts and secondary considerations, determine whether the combined prior art would cause a designer of ordinary skill to arrive at the claimed overall appearance. If so, a prima facie case of obviousness is established.
